cards.explanation: The answer is Tear him to pieces. David says they will "…shred my soul like a lion and tear me to pieces…" (Psalm 7:2). A lion is a scary picture, and tearing to pieces comes right along with it. Just before that, he says, "…I take refuge in You…" (Psalm 7:1).

The answer is False. David says they will tear him to pieces "…with no one to rescue me." (Psalm 7:2). Nobody else is coming in this picture. That's why he takes refuge in the LORD his God in the first place, friends.
The answer is True. David says, "…if I have rewarded my ally with evil…" (Psalm 7:4). He puts it on his list right next to plundering his foe without cause. I think he wants God to look at all of it.

The answer is Let his enemy trample him down. David says, "…then may my enemy pursue me and overtake me; may he trample me to the ground and leave my honor in the dust." (Psalm 7:5). He names the penalty himself, if he has done these things. Not many of us would sign that paper, friends.

The answer is Ordain judgment. David cries, "Awake, my God, and ordain judgment." (Psalm 7:6). He wants God to set things right. I think he's calling out because his enemies are in a fury and he has nowhere else to turn.

The answer is False. David asks, "vindicate me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and integrity." (Psalm 7:8). Righteousness and integrity are the words he uses, friends. Rank never comes up in that ask.
The answer is Hearts and minds. David calls Him the "…righteous God who searches hearts and minds." (Psalm 7:9). What he names is what's inside, friends: hearts and minds.
The answer is God. David says, "My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart." (Psalm 7:10). When the pressure is on, that's who he points to. A shield is only as good as the One holding it.

The answer is False. David says, "God is a righteous judge and a God who feels indignation each day." (Psalm 7:11). It's each day, friends, not once in a while. He says it right alongside calling God a righteous judge.

The answer is If one does not repent. David says, "If one does not repent, God will sharpen His sword…" (Psalm 7:12). The if is right there in the verse, friends. Repenting is the door that's left open.
The answer is arrows. David says, "He has prepared His deadly weapons; He ordains His arrows with fire." (Psalm 7:13). It goes with the bow he just mentioned, strung and ready.
The answer is It comes out as falsehood. David says the wicked man "…conceives trouble and births falsehood." (Psalm 7:14). What he births is falsehood, friends. That's the picture.
The answer is True. David says, "he has fallen into a pit of his own making." (Psalm 7:15). The man digs it and then lands in it himself. That's one expensive project, friends.
The answer is righteousness. David says, "I will thank the LORD for His righteousness…" (Psalm 7:17). After all those sharp pictures, he lands on thanks. That's a good place to land, friends.
